status: planned; no new Issue 16 images generated or approved
character_design: Q retains approved narrow segmented head, round ear mechanisms, exposed neck, question-mark breastplate, long worn coat and supported knee. Chano and Lucía follow their approved references. Custodian is a tall man about sixty, long tied-back gray hair, glasses, white work shirt and boots: he testifies in person, then speaks by phone after watching the replay. Hilario is the water vendor seen remotely, not retired miner Don Hilario.
art_direction: Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, pure white highlights, no sepia or cream ink wash. Full bleed at comic trim, separate typeset caption margin. Near-future Mexican hearing in a renovated cinema, not a purportedly documented real courtroom or a medieval inquisition. Nine unique exact-facing scenes plus cover. No readable protected records, no illustration of the invented turbine charge as an actual event, no seizure of the already delivered module.
approval_scope: Source-bound planning only: 20-page internal layout proof, 10 planned plates, 10 A3 landscape sides on 5 short-edge duplex sheets. Georgia 12.4/17.5667 pt. Exact facing text and scene anchors refreshed after return/hearing pacing revision. No new artwork, final illustrated PDF, literary-grade certification or print job. The delivered module and retained original papers do not enter Castalia's transport or Q's hearing folder.

plates.caption: The Trial of the Machine
plates.scene_brief: Wide view from the rear seats of the renovated cinema used for the hearing: Q sits among ordinary tables, advisers, clerks and competing stacks of papers, dwarfed by the old screen and theater architecture. Institutional spectacle without a symbolic execution. No chains, lance, giant attack or readable private exhibit. Leave clear space for separately typeset title; use the wide auditorium composition only on this cover.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Sixteen: The Trial
of the Machine
The hearing began with an
argument about which table Q
should occupy. Castalia wanted him
available as a source of evidence
and returned as property. Its
counsel also wanted his
independent decisions
distinguished from the institute's
responsibility for them. The same
independence looked different at
different points in the claim.
Q sat beside his own adviser. The
court had restricted network use
during testimony. He could consult
the permitted local records and ask
for an exhibit, but not conduct a
new search while a witness spoke.
He understood the rule.
Understanding did not stop him
wanting to check one more thing.
Before the first witness he asked the
clerk for something to support his
knee. The clerk found a low stool in
the projection booth. Q moved it
until his foot rested comfortably,
then asked whether it blocked the
aisle. The clerk moved the cable
instead.
The proceedings used a renovated
cinema with an overflow room.
Before they began, the public
stream showed the seal of the
Republic, then a sponsor card on
the broadcaster's own channel. The
judge required the sponsor card
removed from the courtroom feed.
Viewers watching through another
outlet continued to see it beside the
word independent.
Several matters had been scheduled
together for evidence on
overlapping facts: the disputed
custody of Q's body, damage claims,
access to the retained materials,
and the challenge to his removal of
the private retrieval layer. The
hearing would not settle every
question implied by calling a
machine a defendant. It would
produce decisions with
consequences for the machine
sitting at the table.
The first compilation showed Q at
the distribution park, the Isthmus,
the transport frame, and the joint
appearance with Prime. The
sequence offered violence, restraint,
and improvement before any
witness had explained an event.
One item was a promotional
illustration in which Q raised the
brass key toward the turbines.
His adviser asked that the sources
and dates be displayed. The clerk
separated footage, still images, and
promotional reconstruction. The
illustration remained in the record
as evidence of publicity, not a
photograph of the act it depicted.
This distinction made the
plates.caption: A Place at the Table
plates.scene_brief: Before testimony, Q sits beside his female adviser in the renovated cinema, cautiously resting his supported knee and foot on a low projection-booth stool. The clerk moves a cable away from the aisle. Low eye-level framing emphasizes practical accommodation and the distance to the hearing table, not a chained robot or a ritual trial. No turbine attack or invented court costume.
plates.scene_anchor: The clerk moved the cable instead.

plates.facing_text:
compilation less stirring and more
expensive to prepare correctly.
The water receipt entered next. It
supported a purchase at Hilario's
table, not a complete account of the
first sally. Hilario appeared by
video, with his actual stock of
bottles behind him.
He gave the name on his tax papers
and the name he used at home. The
clerk recorded the connection after
checking the supporting document.
The broadcaster misspelled the
displayed name anyway.
“Who paid?” counsel asked.
“The machine. Cash, after the
reader lost its connection.”
A hand with coins entered the
corner of his picture.
“Cold?” someone asked.
“In the tub under the table.”
Counsel looked up. “Are you
addressing the court?”
“I'm selling water.”
The judge paused the questioning.
Hilario found the change and asked
someone out of view to watch the
table. When he sat down again,
counsel had to ask which question
he had reached. Hilario
remembered.
“Did you see what happened inside
the park?”
“Some of it from the road. More of
it on everyone's telephone
afterward.”
“You wrote that he threatened a
pallet mover.”
“That's what the video looked like.”
“Did you hear him threaten it?”
Hilario moved his cap between his
hands. “Not from my table.”
They compared his letters. His
account of the timing had changed.
He could distinguish the cash
payment he remembered from the
sequence he had later assembled
around it. The judge let counsel
question both without making the
uncertainty disprove the sale.
“Do you see Q acting alone in this
clip?”
“I see the clip leaving Chano out.”
The fuller view showed Chano
directing them toward the exit. It
also showed the cartons damaged
after Q pressed the stop.
Chano testified with his copies and
retention receipts. The original
ledger was still in Tijuana. He
identified its warehouse
acknowledgment and explained
which copies he actually possessed.
When asked whether Q had
promised him a governorship, he
described the breakfast joke and the
plates.caption: Cold Water, Live Evidence
plates.scene_brief: View from the hearing room toward the video display: water vendor Hilario at his roadside stock of bottles, making change for a customer's hand entering the picture. The tub of cold bottles is under his table. Counsel pauses in the foreground. Hilario is remote, not physically at the hearing; do not confuse him with retired miner Don Hilario or place Q at the stall.
plates.scene_anchor: Hilario found the change and asked someone out of view to watch the table.

plates.facing_text:
later paid agreement for traveling
together.
“You accepted payment from him?”
“Yes.”
“So you had an interest in
continuing the journey.”
“Yes. I also had interests before I
met him.”
Counsel asked about the transport
frame. Chano said he caught the
technician's arm when Q fell and
released it when told. The full
record and the technician's
statement were considered
alongside the short clip. Chano
asked to see the fall at its ordinary
speed. Slowed down, it had given
him far more time to decide what to
do than he remembered having.
The clerk played it again.
“Was Q your employer, your
companion, or your friend?”
“He paid me. We travelled together.
He's my friend.”
“All three?”
“You asked three things.”
Chano looked toward Q after
answering. Q had been prepared for
a useful account of their agreement
and found himself unexpectedly
grateful for the third sentence.
During the recess he caught Chano
by the water dispenser.
“Thank you for that.”
“Which part?”
“The third one.”
Chano held out a paper cup. “I
meant the others too.”
Álvaro Mena testified about the
wind enterprise. He said Q had
announced an attack on giants.
Asked where he stood when he
heard it, he described the arrival
area. Asked which recording
contained the announcement, he
pointed to the promotional image.
“That image contains no sound,”
Q's adviser said.
“It reflects the event.”
“It reflects an account of the event.
Which words did you hear?”
Álvaro asked to review the arrival
footage. Beto's voice called the
turbines giants. Q answered about
the archive's electricity supply.
Later footage showed him asking
when the gate would open. The
microphone did not capture every
exchange in the crowd.
“Then I may have combined the
later account with what I
remember,” Álvaro said.
Q looked down at the illustration in
his own bundle. He had seen it
often enough to know the pose
better than he remembered where
plates.caption: The Third Answer
plates.scene_brief: During the hearing recess Chano offers Q a paper cup beside an ordinary water dispenser. Two companions, slight smile and unceremonious posture, no consoling embrace or heroic benediction. Keep the worn coat, mechanical hand and practical knee support. Chano has copies and a folder, not the original Tijuana ledger.
plates.scene_anchor: Chano held out a paper cup.

plates.facing_text:
his hands had actually been. He
turned the sheet over.
Teresa, the shift engineer, identified
her operator-requested stop of the
nearest group. The record did not
show Q sending a shutdown
command. She explained the
visitor-boundary problem and
confirmed that other machines
continued operating. Q had
remained inside the marked bay
and asked the guard to help the
woman through. The photographer
had left to compose his own picture.
“Was a precautionary stop
justified?” counsel asked.
“On the information I had, yes.”
“Does that establish every loss
claimed afterward?”
“No. That's not what the operating
record calculates.”
The consortium's claimed losses,
the gate arrangement, and the
publicity permissions were
examined separately. The released
record concerning its later brief was
attributed to its source. Bixha's
position appeared through the
material she had authorized for this
proceeding, not as a summary Q
had composed in the witness chair.
The Custodian followed. His long
hair was tied back; his glasses
rested halfway down his nose while
he read the original leave
authorization. He had brought the
document whose significance had
grown while its words stayed still.
“Did you authorize Q's first
journey?”
“Yes.”
“Did you believe you had authority
to do so?”
“Yes. The scope of that authority is
now disputed.”
“Did you intend him to leave
without permission?”
“No. We agreed on a day trip,
money, and a call. I gave him the
release. I didn't set a test he could
pass only by disobeying me.”
Castalia's counsel distinguished
permission to leave the site from
authority to dispose of a body
claimed as an institutional asset.
The Custodian had not transferred
title in a coat pocket. He had let Q
go into the world, and had not
examined all the powers that could
be used to bring him back.
He described the archive's changing
purposes: preservation, research
access, valuation, and a public
product. Where he knew who
approved a change, he gave the
name and the document. Where he
did not, he said so. Several
omissions were his own failures to
ask for the underlying record.
plates.caption: The Original Permission
plates.scene_brief: Tall male Custodian gives evidence in person, long gray hair tied back and glasses halfway down his nose, reading his original day-trip authorization. White work shirt, ordinary table and papers, restrained theater fixtures behind him. Q can be seen seated with his adviser in the side distance. Do not make the Custodian female, bald, a robed judge or a remote video witness; the document is permission to leave, not a transfer of ownership.
plates.scene_anchor: His long hair was tied back; his glasses rested halfway down his nose

plates.facing_text:
The broadcaster cut away during
part of the list. The court record
retained it.
Lucía gave evidence on the
particular encounters and handling
records she had agreed to address.
Asked whether Q contained a
human soul, she said that was not
something she could establish. The
judge directed the questioner back
to observed actions.
“Did he listen when you refused the
role he offered?”
“He didn't offer it. Someone in the
audience did. We both said no.”
“Did he later expose information
about your work?”
“He gave my name in the interview
while trying to correct the story.
That gave it another way to find
me.”
“And used your private inquiry as
an example at the university?”
“No. I was beside the door when
they asked him. He said the
requests weren't his to discuss and
put his own opening on the screen.”
Q put the seminar's exhibit
reference beside his adviser's hand.
She requested the permitted clip. It
showed the paragraph, then a
student asking to finish reading it
before the explanation continued.
The clerk entered the example
separately from the interview.
“You also used his presence to
attract funding?” counsel asked.
“Yes. I told the donors he would be
working at the archive before
asking him. He objected when they
asked for a demonstration.”
“But gave one.”
“After we spoke. Twenty minutes on
the work, without recording or
endorsement. He left when he said
he would.”
Counsel asked whether the donors
had contributed. She identified the
two receipts and the amended
budget. Paid hours and equipment
had different entries; she pointed to
each.
The evidence concerning the
university distinguished Q's public
recommendation from the private
application review and the later
leak. The miner's permission
accompanied his selected pension
pages. Alma's handling receipt
recorded the return of her
photograph; the exhibit was the
public article, not her original.
Each distinction took time. Viewers
in the overflow room went out for
food and returned to discover that
nothing had happened except
several important things had ceased
to be called the same thing.
plates.caption: The Example on the Screen
plates.scene_brief: During Lucía's evidence, Q places the permitted seminar exhibit reference beside his female adviser's hand. Lucía remains at the witness table in the middle distance; the clerk prepares the already permitted clip. Composition uses hands and sight lines rather than a collage of earlier adventures. The projected material is Q's own prose, not Lucía's private inquiry, a family photograph or the restricted lease. No readable confidential documents.
plates.scene_anchor: Q put the seminar's exhibit reference beside his adviser's hand.

plates.facing_text:
Q had discussed testifying with his
adviser. He understood the risk of
giving a fluent answer that seemed
broader than the evidence
supporting it. He chose to answer
the specified matters anyway. The
adviser kept the documents within
reach and told him to ask for the
question again if a neat sentence
concealed more than one premise.
He confirmed both Q and the
registered serial designation. He
did not need to deny the number in
order to dispute Castalia's claim to
the body bearing it.
“Did you understand the media
license?” counsel asked.
“I understood the terms we
negotiated, including the
private-manuscript exclusion. I
underestimated some uses of the
recordings. I also wanted the repair,
travel, and audience the
arrangement offered.”
“You signed to protect Chano?”
“That was one consideration. He
told me not to use it as the whole
explanation.”
“Did you cause damage at the
distribution park?”
“I pressed the stop because I
couldn't see whether Chano was
clear. The operator's log showed
that the brake had already engaged.
Two cartons were damaged in the
interruption I caused. I accept that.
I don't know that every later loss in
the claim follows from it.”
“Were you authorized to enter?”
“To reception, along the marked
walk. Lety confirmed that over the
intercom. We hadn't reached the
hatch when it happened.”
His adviser asked for the entry
audio and the operator's record to
be considered with the camera
view. On the screen, the trailer hid
Chano again. Q knew now where he
had been. He waited for the image
to catch up.
The questioner returned to the
wind farm. Q described the gate,
the woman, the visitor boundary,
and the call he had not heard
clearly. Lucía had repeated the
instruction; the guard had held the
gate. Q had not crossed the line or
attended as a representative of the
community. The photographer's
route came from the later staff
report; Q did not claim to have
watched it from the gate.
“Did you decide the turbines were
enemies?”
“No. They supplied electricity to the
archive where I was made. That
relationship was part of what I went
there to examine.”
“But the giant image was useful to
your story.”
plates.caption: The View and the Record
plates.scene_brief: Q gives evidence about the distribution-park stop while his adviser requests entry audio and the operator's record alongside the camera view. Frame from the side with Q, permitted papers within reach, and a screen whose industrial camera still includes an obstructing trailer. Do not depict the later brake log as something Q saw in the original incident or show a heroic charge. Distinct from the seminar exhibit hand gesture.
plates.scene_anchor: His adviser asked for the entry audio and the operator's record to be considered with the camera view.

plates.facing_text:
“It was useful to several stories.
That doesn't make it a record of
what my hand did.”
He was asked about the removal of
the private index. The audit record
established the scope and checks;
the underlying deposits had not
been erased from their keepers'
storage. The opposing parties
disputed authority and claimed loss
of a valuable access arrangement.
“You made yourself less capable?”
“I removed a capability whose
permissions were being challenged,
under the reviewed procedure. I can
still answer for the acts I remember
and the records available here. I
can't replace the removed material
by guessing.”
“Could you recreate it from what
you learned?”
“Not as a verified reconstruction.
Some general knowledge remains.
Some connections were stored in
that layer. Treating my plausible
answer as the missing record would
create another problem, not restore
the original.”
The questioner displayed the
limited appearance agreement
beside Q HAS CHOSEN
CONTINUITY. Q read the
attached statement he had signed.
The linked qualification was part of
the agreement even if most viewers
had not clicked it. The court had the
whole page.
Then came the question about
Lucía: had he loved her?
His adviser objected to its
relevance. The judge permitted only
a question about the public role and
representation that formed part of
the submitted material.
“The comparison came from the
audience at her reading,” Q said.
“She rejected it; so did I. I had used
the same nickname in a private
note, and Chano copied it into a
register. We crossed it out. At the
interview I gave her name while
trying to correct the story. That
brought more attention to her. It
didn't give me a right to speak for
her.”
The questioner asked whether he
still wished to become human. Q
looked at the permitted notes, then
left them where they were.
“I still want to live, meet people,
and finish the account I'm writing
with the Custodian. I began by
calling that becoming human. I
haven't found a better short phrase
for all of it. The phrase doesn't
excuse what I've done.”
For once nobody in the room tried
to improve his answer into a
definition before the next question
arrived.
plates.caption: What He Still Wants
plates.scene_brief: Closer, quiet portrait at the hearing: Q has looked at his notes and left them on the table while answering what he still wants. Face attentive to a person beyond frame; relaxed open mechanical hands, worn coat and unaltered head construction. No human soul escaping the body, no erasure of his mind, no broken corpse or triumphant declaration of universal legal personhood. His desire to live and write is an answer, not a coronation.
plates.scene_anchor: Q looked at the permitted notes, then left them where they were.

plates.facing_text:
The order issued the following day
resolved less than the headlines
called a verdict. Q's admitted part
in the park damage remained
actionable; the broader losses and
allocation of liability required
further determination. The court
did not find that he had remotely
shut down the wind farm. The
access dispute would continue on
the records preserved for it, not by
demanding that Q conjure the
deleted private index during
testimony.
The custody restriction remained
while the body's ownership was
litigated, with accompanied
journeys subject to an approved
schedule and review. Q asked his
adviser how to propose another
journey. She wrote the contact and
required notice beside the condition
on his copy.
The community archive's records
were to be preserved for a defined
inspection proposal. Lucía's adviser
sought limits on access and copying
before any transfer. The sealed
third-party module had already
reached its appointed receiver in
Tijuana. Its completed receipt did
not entitle Castalia to the
testimony. The judge left any
further request for that deposit to a
separate application, not the claim
over Q's body and coat.
The separate review of Chano's
intervention closed without a
charge after the fuller account was
considered. Chano received the
notice and read it twice.
He had wanted to tear up the earlier
notice. Lucía asked him to keep
both. This was beginning to seem to
him the archive's most reliable way
of spoiling a celebration.
Prime sent Q a private message
asking whether he wanted to talk,
not a broadcast declaring the
proceeding a success. Q said yes,
after the call to the Custodian. After
the hearing's questions, he still
wanted to hear someone address
him without putting the answer in
evidence.
Lucía handed him a folder for the
copies he could take. On the tab she
had written Q - UNFINISHED.
On the back of the schedule inside
it, he noted the next preparation
meeting and the writing session he
had postponed. Then he called the
Custodian.
“I've been watching the replay,” the
Custodian said.
“Did your version have the
sponsor?”
“Until I found the other channel.”
“Keep that detail. I haven't got an
ending for today.”
plates.caption: Another Appointment
plates.scene_brief: After the following day's interim order, Lucía hands Q a folder for authorized copies. His schedule lies inside, with a next preparation meeting and postponed writing session; Chano keeps two notices nearby rather than tearing one up. The Custodian is not beside them in this scene: the subsequent call concerns his viewing a replay. Do not put the sealed module or original Tijuana ledger in this folder; do not depict release from all restrictions. Typeset any essential folder label separately.
plates.scene_anchor: Lucía handed him a folder for the copies he could take.

plates.facing_text:
“Have you eaten?”
Q looked toward Chano, who was
already asking the clerk which exit
led to the food stalls. “We're
working on it.”
Interlude: The Form
Without a Category
The tribunal secretary tried to close
the administrative entry before
lunch. The matter itself was not
closed, but the entry required a
category for the party whose status
the order had declined to settle in
general.
He chose the procedural role under
which Q had appeared and attached
the relevant qualification. The
public summary field still offered
only person or property. He
referred that mismatch to the
supervisor instead of deciding an
unresolved question with his
mouse.
“It won't publish without a
selection,” his assistant said.
“Then that part waits.”
The assistant looked at the tamal
sandwich on the desk. “Does that
wait too?”
The secretary moved it away from
the copier. The machine had
already produced one sheet
containing the shadow of a napkin.
He was not prepared to add lunch
to the matters for which the office
might later need a correction.
They prepared an interim cover
sheet that identified the proceeding
by number and referred readers to
the order for the unresolved status.
The absence of a one-word answer
did not make the file inaccessible. It
did leave a space where a
broadcaster could supply one of its
own.
Chano collected the copies for
which he had a receipt. The
secretary gave him the extra cover
sheet and pointed out that it was
not the order itself. Chano put it in
his folder, not the ledger still in
Tijuana.
Outside, a vendor sold him a tamal
sandwich. Chano had the folder
under one arm and the sandwich in
his other hand when his phone
rang.
“Let it ring,” he said to Lucía.
“It might be important.”
“Then they'll ring again.”
He took a bite. Inside, the secretary
finally did the same.
plates.caption: The Shadow of a Napkin
plates.scene_brief: Tribunal back office: the secretary moves his tamal sandwich away from a copier while the assistant points toward the lunch. A fresh output sheet bears the faint shadow of a napkin, not legible evidence. Mundane office light and delicately comic hand positions; no magical talking copier and no new judgment printed by accident. Q need not appear in a scene he does not witness. Distinct from the courtroom and water-dispenser plates.
plates.scene_anchor: The machine had already produced one sheet containing the shadow of a napkin.
